title: Optional cloud lab — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a learner has no Azure subscription. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud what the simulated lab does prove and what it does not, without letting the listener assume a real deployment.

vocabulary.meaning: the exact set of behaviours a local stand-in reproduces, outside of which its results say nothing
a part of a procedure that was never executed, and which an honest report names instead of implying

expectedElements: What the simulation proves is bounded explicitly
At least one unproven step is named
What would close the gap is stated concretely
modelAnswer: The lab runs against a local simulation, and I want to be precise about what that proves. The evidence it produces is a syntactically valid deployment definition and scripts that run end to end. It does not prove that the cloud provider accepts the definition, that the quotas allow it, or that the network rules behave as written. Those three are unproven, and I would not report them as working. Closing the gap needs one real subscription and one real run, and it would take about a day. Should I request a temporary subscription for that?
commonMistakes: Letting the audience assume a simulated run is a deployment
Naming the gap without saying what would close it
variants: Answer again to a learner who asks whether the certificate still counts.
